quote.text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
quote.author: Seneca, “Letters to Lucilius,” Letter II (c. 65 AD)

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · The suit, from the canvas up
stories.headline: A jacket is not fabric — it is fabric hung on a skeleton, and the skeleton is the whole game
stories.dek: Learn one thing — how the chest is built — and you can judge any suit on any rack, cold. Then learn one number, the weight, and buy the only suit Singapore needs.

stories.headline: The oval on the table that becomes a world — four hobbies wearing one set of tracks
stories.dek: A layout starts as a locomotive, a few wagons and a circle of track in a box. It ends, for the properly hooked, as a room — because model railways are engineering, craft, collecting and operations at once, and each one has no bottom.

stories.kicker: Iran & the Gulf · The second gate, and a first hint of talks
stories.headline: Both doors to the oil are contested — then, on Friday, a door opens in Oman
stories.dek: A week that completed the Houthi grip on the Red Sea gate ended on the first genuine de-escalation signal since February: Iran will meet the Gulf states in Muscat on Monday, and Brent gave back three per cent on the news.

stories.kicker: The haze & the pay debate · What it means for your Sunday
stories.headline: The rain bought back the weekend — but the dry spell isn’t finished, and neither is the argument about disclosure
stories.dek: Friday’s showers pulled the air back into the healthy band after the first “unhealthy” reading since 2023; and the Workers’ Party backed the pay rise while pressing the one demand that actually bites — show us the real numbers.

stories.kicker: The summit clock · Xi to Washington, 24 September
stories.headline: The twenty-five-per-cent chip deal is delivering almost nothing — and China’s own silicon is scaling to fill the gap
stories.dek: With Xi Jinping bound for Washington in a fortnight and Nvidia’s China business the top item, the reopened H200 channel has become a stalemate neither side is filling — while Huawei and Cambricon ship the domestic stack.

stories.kicker: Gear We’re Watching · The anti-disposable headphone
stories.headline: A wireless can you can actually fix — Beyerdynamic bets a buy-once reader will pay for a replaceable battery
stories.dek: Most wireless headphones die the day their glued-in battery does. The Aventho Y, launched at IFA, ships with a user-replaceable battery, magnetic ear cushions and ninety hours of play — the buy-once case, at a mainstream price.

stories.kicker: Objects & Escapes · Fifty years of light
stories.headline: The watch that never needs winding, or a battery, turns fifty — and Citizen marks it with paper and light
stories.dek: Eco-Drive is the quiet buy-once story in watches: a movement powered by any light, sealed for decades, needing nothing. For its half-century Citizen offers a hand-dyed Japanese-paper dial in titanium, and a new light-powered calibre.

stories.kicker: Culture Desk · The Lido hands out its Lion
stories.headline: “Woman Unknown” takes the Golden Lion, Malkovich the actor’s cup — and our own call comes good
stories.dek: Venice closed on Saturday with the Golden Lion to May el-Toukhy’s post-war thriller and a rare double for its lead; the festival’s loudest ovation, and John Malkovich’s prize, went to the film we said would not win it.

stories.kicker: Raising Them Well · The law arrives, the evidence complicates it
stories.headline: Singapore is about to draw a line under thirteen — and the research on what phone rules actually do is messier than the headline
stories.dek: Age-assurance becomes law in early 2027: under-thirteens blocked, teens kept only where platforms behave. The best 2026 evidence on school phone bans, though, says the effect on learning is close to zero — useful to know for a girl starting secondary school.

stories.headline: An oil-shock reflation meets a Fed expected to hike — and the ten-year knocks on five per cent
stories.dek: One supply-driven force is running through every instrument this week: a spiking oil price is colliding with a central bank leaning to tighten, pushing long yields toward five, keeping the dollar firm, and pressuring risk while gold holds its bid.

stories.kicker: The Long Game · The grip and the engine
stories.headline: Why a handshake predicts your decade — and why Zone 2 is a base, not a magic bullet
stories.dek: Two of the strongest longevity markers a mid-forties reader can actually train are grip strength and cardiorespiratory fitness. The 2026 research strengthens both — and quietly deflates the idea that slow cardio alone is enough.

stories.headline: Thailand shortens its welcome, Scoot adds a China city, and a new gate to Sydney opens
stories.dek: The weekend’s most SG-relevant travel change lands the day this issue prints: Thailand cuts its visa-free stay in half. Plus new routes, a slipping SIA seat, and a strike weekend in Europe.

stories.kicker: What’s Worth Booking · The dated agenda
stories.headline: A Grand Prix with a Sprint, a snow festival to fly for, and Westlife’s return
Streedhan goes to work
stories.dek: India is quietly liquefying its last taboo asset. The family gold — a woman’s own, inherited mother to daughter — is being turned into working cash at industrial scale, and the shame has flipped to savvy. It is 1991, rerun at the scale of the household.
